results.content: President Trump’s approval rating dipped again this week, following a downward trend in support for the president amid the ongoing Iran war and mounting affordability concerns ahead of November’s midterms. The latest survey from The Economist/YouGov, published Monday, found 33 percent of respondents said they approved of how Trump has handled his job as president. Support for the president was split largely along partisan lines, with 79 percent of GOP respondents and only 4 percent of Democratic respondents approving of Trump’s job performance, according to the poll. results.content: President Donald Trump has broken his own record for the lowest approval rating recorded by The Economist/YouGov, with just 33 percent of Americans now saying they approve of the way he is handling his job as president. What To Know The significance of the latest result is ultimately less about one number than about the trajectory. Trump Hits New Lows Among Key Blocs Trump’s approval is also reaching new lows across several key voting blocs. Trump has a new net approval low among white Americans too, with a 39 percent approval in the new poll compared to 57 percent disapproval. results.content: # Trump approval rating sinks to yet another low in new poll. President Donald Trump’s polling woes continue as he fell to a new record low since his return to the White House, according to a new Reuters/Ipsos survey, with only one in three Americans approving of his job performance. The poll, released on Aug. 17, found that only 33% of Americans approved of Trump’s performance, down 2 percentage points from another Reuters/Ipsos poll from earlier this month. Trump’s performance on the Aug. 17 poll marks the lowest approval rating the president has seen in Reuters/Ipsos tracking since his return to the White House in 2025.
